question: Should ClawHub establish an advisory-first capability declaration contract, and if so which limited vocabulary, declaration authority, and legacy/unknown behavior should be public before scanner or install-policy integration begins?
rationale: The remaining work defines a public trust boundary and may influence moderation and downstream install-policy consumers; code inspection cannot safely choose those semantics or their migration policy.

options.title: Approve an advisory-only v1 contract
options.body: Specify a bounded versioned vocabulary, preserve an explicit unknown state for legacy skills, validate declarations at publish time, and surface discrepancies only as review evidence.

options.title: Defer until review policy is defined
options.body: Keep existing metadata and scanning evidence separate until maintainers first approve the mismatch policy and user-facing trust presentation.

options.title: Limit v1 to existing metadata
options.body: Standardize only dependencies and environment declarations now, while reserving execution, filesystem, network, and secret claims for a later security design.

recommendation.title: Approve an advisory-only v1 contract
recommendation.body: Specify a bounded versioned vocabulary, preserve an explicit unknown state for legacy skills, validate declarations at publish time, and surface discrepancies only as review evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior capability-schema proposal and member-associated repository work make them the strongest available routing candidate for the contract discussion.
